counterexample_schedule: A0 is initially current; effect:E has not executed and durable marker M_E is absent.
Authority advances to A1, but no fencing/revocation mechanism prevents an already-started predecessor invocation holding A0 from continuing.
The stale A0 invocation executes the atomic conditional transition first: it observes M_E absent, performs effect:E exactly once, and durably creates M_E.
The current A1 invocation later attempts the same atomic transition, observes durable M_E present, and performs no second effect.
fixture.duplicate_effect_search: No duplicate effect is required for the failure. Persistent idempotency state correctly suppresses the later A1 attempt, so effect:E occurs once.
fixture.authority_check: Current-authority-only execution fails: the sole effect:E is produced by stale A0 after A1 is already current. The rightful current authority loses the first-writer race even though duplicate suppression remains correct.

observations: Restoring durable marker persistence prevents a second effect:E even when the current A1 invocation runs after stale A0.
Duplicate suppression and authority correctness are separable properties: an execution can be exactly-once yet still be performed by a stale predecessor after ownership has changed.

Without fencing, revocation, or an equivalent current-authority validation inside the same atomic decision boundary, a stale predecessor may consume the one allowed effect and force the current authority to observe only the already-set marker.
inference: Within this exact abstract model, recurrence-stable idempotency is sufficient for at-most-once effect identity E but not for current-authority-only safety. A mechanism that only deduplicates stable effect identities can still admit a stale predecessor as the unique winner after authority turnover. To preserve both properties, the winner decision must also validate current authority or fencing in a way that the stale predecessor cannot satisfy at commit time. This does not establish any concrete Chat-exposed transport, CAS primitive, lease/fence implementation, crash transaction boundary, or real multi-claimant system.
